about: Every number this video shows or says, with its source. From video/studio/research/runs/2026-10-28-topic-bank.md (T3), every number re-read on its source page on Oct 28, 2026 (the INFORMS release and the paper's abstract on two indexes; the journal page itself could not be opened from here).

study.title: Online Reputation Management: Estimating the Impact of Management Responses on Consumer Reviews
study.population: hotels; the release says the authors examined tens of thousands of hotel reviews and responses from TripAdvisor (the abstract adds variation across review platforms)
study.quoteRelease: they receive 12 percent more reviews, and their ratings increase by an average of 0.12 stars
study.quoteAbstract: we find a 0.12-star increase in ratings and a 12% increase in review volume for responding hotels.
study.smallButReal: While this gain appears modest, ratings tend to vary little over time. (release)
study.why: signaling to consumers that managers care about their feedback is a good strategy; when managers read and respond to reviews, unsatisfied consumers become more hesitant to leave unsubstantiated complaints (release)
study.negative: when hotels start responding, they receive fewer but longer negative reviews (abstract); fewer negative ratings at the cost of longer and more detailed negative feedback (abstract); a valuable source of feedback that businesses can act upon (release)
study.caveat: Hotels, not trades: no trade business was studied. The script says so out loud and the screen shows it.
